facts: Funes exposes a database-backed ObservationStore through Laravel's container.
Observation acceptance, payload preservation, canonical resource creation, and discovery creation occur in one transaction.
Raw payloads are content-addressed by SHA-256 and remain recoverable through observations.
Extraction successes and failures are immutable records keyed by observation, extractor, and extractor version.
A canonical resource and payload hash identify one historical effect; a new payload hash creates a new observation.
Observation acceptance returns an explicit first, unchanged, or changed disposition.
Discovery provenance is queryable from a child resource back to its parent resource and observation.
Landing is the complete master application schema and source of truth for shared database vocabulary; Funes only appends prefixed history tables.
Funes exposes portable entity reference kinds for projects, identities, repositories, organizations, and domains.

Every accepted observation returns append-only provenance assertions containing a resolvable source locator, producer identity, occurrence time when known, observation time, recording time, and transformation lineage.
An exact retry reuses its provenance assertion; a later encounter with identical content appends provenance without duplicating the historical observation.
Acceptance-gateway replay resolves the accepted observation and its provenance.
Entity kind, source reference, and external identifier resolve to one stable Funes entity reference.
Repeated identity claims reuse the entity and provenance evidence; later observations append evidence without duplicating the entity.
Identity queries return preserved external identifiers and provenance by either source identity or stable Funes reference.
Observations are explicitly typed observed; extraction results are explicitly typed derived.
Every derived extraction result names its evidence observation and a non-empty, versioned derivation process.
The observation acceptance seam rejects derived results by concrete type.
Every new observation provenance assertion requires a stable ingestion-run reference alongside producer identity.
Every new derived record requires producer identity and ingestion-run context, and retrieval returns every known context.
A later producer run yielding the same derived result appends provenance without duplicating the result.
Structured observation metadata is preserved as append-only namespaced and schema-versioned assertions linked to provenance.
Metadata changes append assertions without changing observation identity, while exact assertion retries deduplicate.
Pre-contract observation JSON is returned under the explicit funes:legacy metadata namespace without rewriting stored history.
Historical text is preserved as immutable namespaced assertions linked to observation provenance.
Textual raw payloads are exposed as funes:source-payload assertions whose content identity is the payload hash.
The text projection is disposable and rebuilds completely from authoritative observations, payloads, and text assertions.
Cross-package references serialize owner, object type, stable identifier, optional object version, and optional provenance reference under contract version 1.
Mixed reference batches are grouped and resolved once per owning package with explicit outcomes for every requested reference.
Aleph observation and artifact references and Kilgore interpretation references pass the shared contract without model imports or private-table access.
Historical observations return typed subject, actor, context, artifact, and target associations to durable cross-package entity references.
Entity association facts deduplicate independently from their append-only source provenance.
Exact durable entity references traverse back to associated historical observations.
Historical observations preserve related, references, responds-to, corrects, and supersedes links as target references rather than embedded records.
Historical relationship facts deduplicate independently from append-only relationship provenance.
Incoming and outgoing historical relationships are retrievable in deterministic order.
Caused-by and child-of relationships require a preserved namespaced source field and declared value.
Explicit causal and parent declarations retain the observation provenance that supplied them and remain idempotent across retries.

Cross-package events serialize stable identity, producer, type, version, temporal coordinates, subject references, causation, correlation, provenance, source metadata, payload, and optional stream position under contract version 1.
Event identity is the consumer idempotency key, while a fingerprint of the complete immutable envelope exposes conflicting reuse.
Delivery attempts are immutable records separate from event facts and represent started, succeeded, retryable-failure, or dead-lettered outcomes.
Ordering exists only within an explicitly named durable stream; cross-stream and global ordering are not defined.
Aleph observation, Titan work-lifecycle, and Logres runtime fixtures round-trip through the same event envelope.
Funes may preserve accepted event facts and provenance without owning transport retries or current execution lifecycle state.

HistoricalAssertionContract is the provider-neutral contract for one durable claim: subject reference, stable lowercase predicate, JSON-encodable value, source locator, tenant scope, temporal coordinates, provenance, and evidence.

AbstractHistoricalAssertion owns canonical identity, invariants, temporal semantics, and the versioned serialization boundary, and is the only direct parent for provider-family assertion abstractions.
An assertion's type is fixed by its subclass through an abstract assertionType(), so observed, declared, and inferred are distinct classes rather than a mutable field.
Inferred historical assertions require non-empty evidence; observed and declared assertions do not.
Historical assertion occurrence, observation, and recording times remain distinct and must be chronological, and occurrence may be unknown.
A historical assertion fingerprint digests the durable fact and excludes the assertion id, observation time, and recording time, so a re-encounter of the same claim deduplicates.
Historical assertions serialize as a sifrious.historical-assertion document at contract version 1, and a serialized assertion cannot be decoded by a class of a different assertion type.
Concerns are stateless capability interfaces in Sifrious\Funes\Concern; they declare no properties, so composition cannot duplicate state an object already owns.
HistoricalAssertion composes HasStableIdentity, HasProvenance, HasTemporalCoordinates, HasTenantScope, and HasEvidence.
The ten concerns HistoricalAssertion does not compose are recorded in docs/concerns.md with a reason and the owner that does hold each one.
docs/concerns.md carries an invariant-ownership table in which every historical assertion invariant has exactly one owner.
SerializesTemporalCoordinates supplies the shared chronology rule and the microsecond-precision temporal wire format to historical substrate objects.
HasStableIdentity exposes stableIdentity() rather than an object-specific accessor because the concern is shared across every historical substrate object.
ObservedHistoricalAssertion, DeclaredHistoricalAssertion, and InferredHistoricalAssertion are the three concrete assertion classes; each fixes one assertion type and adds nothing else.
HistoricalAssertion has no provider-family layer, because assertion type and provider family are independent axes and an AI-model-sourced claim may be observed, declared, or inferred.
A test walks src/Assertion and fails on any concrete class extending another concrete class.
A test pins the canonical serialized key set, so provider payloads cannot leak into the Funes representation.
The three assertion subclasses are freely substitutable: the same contract behavior, key order, and round trip hold for each.
An inheritance chain partitions exactly one axis; a second independent axis goes into composition or an acquisition adapter.
docs/concerns.md names the axis each MME-2437 substrate object's subclasses partition and whether a provider family applies.
HistoricalRelationshipAssertion partitions the same observed, declared, inferred axis as HistoricalAssertion, so it takes no provider family either.
HistoricalEvent is the substrate object whose subclasses genuinely partition an acquisition-family axis, so the AiModel and Claude layers belong there.
The EventAcceptance and SnapshotObjectReference design notes list subclasses that partition by storage mechanism, contradicting their own invariant that persistence is supplied through adapters.
This package already puts storage behind interfaces: SqlObservationStore, SqlAcceptanceGateway, and SqlHistoricalAppender each implement an interface rather than extend a domain class.
HistoricalAssertionStore is the durable system of record for canonical historical assertions, bound in the container to SqlHistoricalAssertionStore.
Assertion appends are idempotent by fingerprint and return an explicit first or duplicate disposition; a duplicate returns the assertion already stored.
Reusing one assertion identity for a different claim raises AssertionConflict rather than overwriting.
Assertion reads are scoped to the caller's tenant and report another tenant's evidence as absent rather than forbidden, so existence does not leak.
Appending into a tenant the caller does not hold raises UnauthorizedAssertion explicitly.
asOf() reconstructs by transaction time: the latest assertion recorded at or before a moment, with tombstones applying only from when they were recorded.
An assertion withdrawal is an append-only tombstone requiring a reason; the assertion row is never deleted and a repeated tombstone preserves the original.
Assertion timestamp columns are written as UTC strings at microsecond precision because the database driver's binding format truncates to whole seconds.
HistoricalAssertionCodec holds the assertion type-to-class map so the base class does not know its own subclasses.
StoredTimestamp is the single authority for writing a moment to a Funes column and reading it back; stores bind its output rather than a date object.
Stored moments are normalized to UTC at microsecond precision so columns stay lexicographically comparable across source offsets.
The database driver's own date binding formatted values in their arriving timezone and truncated to whole seconds, so one instant reported through two offsets was stored as two different instants.
Reads previously parsed stored timestamps in the process's ambient timezone, so the recovered instant depended on where the code ran.
The 2026_09_02_010000 migration raises all twenty-three pre-existing Funes timestamp columns to precision 6.
Rows written before the precision migration keep whatever fidelity they were stored with; lost offsets are not recoverable and are not guessed.
HistoricalRelationDraft carries occurredAt as a string and is normalized through StoredTimestamp::normalize(), which rejects an unusable moment.
A test asserts that no Sql* store binds a raw date or value to a *_at column.
No backfill or data-quality marker is planned for history written before the timestamp precision fix; existing Funes data is not yet significant and the earlier fidelity is accepted.
assumptions: Crawler-provided source and canonical resource references are stable opaque strings.
A new extraction outcome for the same extractor requires a new extractor version.
Funes history recorded before 2026-09-02 is development data that no consumer depends on.

decisions.decision: Use Laravel's query builder and package migrations as the first persistence implementation.
decisions.rationale: The package already targets Laravel, and a second persistence implementation is not yet demonstrated.

decisions.decision: Treat conflicting reuse of an idempotency reference as an error.
decisions.rationale: Returning an earlier observation for different content would silently lose evidence.

decisions.decision: Keep canonicalization outside Funes.
decisions.rationale: Canonical reference policy belongs to the crawler or connector and is independent of storage.

decisions.decision: Identify observations by canonical resource and content hash.
decisions.rationale: Repeated retrieval of identical content must have one historical effect, while changed content must remain an additional immutable observation.

decisions.decision: Return acceptance disposition with every accepted observation.
decisions.rationale: Callers need to distinguish first, unchanged, and changed content without reconstructing the decision from storage.

decisions.decision: Use landing's names for database concepts shared with Funes.
decisions.rationale: The master schema must retain every landing table and column while Funes adds only new prefixed tables; payload and observation fields therefore use byte_size, content_type, and ingested_at.

decisions.decision: Require entity references to combine a fixed kind with a namespaced opaque identifier.
decisions.rationale: Host database integers and display names cannot preserve identity across application boundaries.

decisions.decision: Store provenance assertions separately from observations.
decisions.rationale: One historical effect may be encountered by multiple producers or at multiple times; preserving those paths must not duplicate or rewrite the observation.

decisions.decision: Resolve stable entities by entity kind, source reference, and exact external identifier.
decisions.rationale: This demonstrated key is stable across historical records and retries without inventing equivalence between unrelated source namespaces.

decisions.decision: Do not infer cross-source identity equivalence.
decisions.rationale: Merging identifiers requires explicit evidence and belongs to the later entity-association contract.

decisions.decision: Keep observed and derived records on separate concrete acceptance seams.
decisions.rationale: A generic record input would permit an interpretation to masquerade as source evidence; explicit types make that invalid state unrepresentable at the package API.

decisions.decision: Require producer identity and ingestion-run reference for new observed and derived records.
decisions.rationale: Producer identity alone cannot distinguish retries, batches, or separate executions by the same connector, process, or agent.

decisions.decision: Backfill pre-contract rows with explicit Funes legacy-run surrogates.
decisions.rationale: A deterministic local surrogate keeps old rows traceable while making no false claim that an unavailable external job identity was recovered.

decisions.decision: Store structured metadata as append-only assertions outside observation identity.
decisions.rationale: Attribute changes must remain recoverable without duplicating or rewriting the source observation.

decisions.decision: Project pre-contract JSON as funes:legacy during retrieval.
decisions.rationale: Read compatibility can preserve original bytes and identify missing historical schema information without a destructive rewrite.

decisions.decision: Keep historical text authoritative and its projection disposable.
decisions.rationale: Text must retain immutable source identity and provenance, while display and future search consumers need a rebuildable document seam rather than ownership of history.

decisions.decision: Defer full-text query behavior and search-engine selection.
decisions.rationale: Stage 1 requires recoverable text and a rebuildable projection seam; ranking, tokenization, and search infrastructure belong to the later index and query stage.

decisions.decision: Represent cross-package identity as a versioned durable reference distinct from display snapshots.
decisions.rationale: Owning packages can change, remove, or restrict current state while historical consumers retain stable identity and the display context observed at the time.

decisions.decision: Route mixed reference batches to owner-controlled resolvers.
decisions.rationale: One batch call per owner prevents N+1 access while leaving authorization and canonical mutable state with the package that owns them.

decisions.decision: Identify entity association facts separately from their provenance links.
decisions.rationale: The same observed relation can be supported by multiple source encounters without duplicating or rewriting the historical fact.

decisions.decision: Represent historical event relationships as typed references with separate provenance.
decisions.rationale: Related records remain canonical and independently retrievable while retries and later evidence do not duplicate or rewrite the relationship fact.

decisions.decision: Require a source declaration for causal and parent-child relationship types.
decisions.rationale: A preserved field locator and declared value distinguish source evidence from an inference based on adjacency or general relatedness.

decisions.decision: Separate immutable cross-package event facts from immutable delivery-attempt records.
decisions.rationale: At-least-once transports need replay-safe event identity while retries, failures, and dead-letter handling evolve without rewriting historical facts or moving execution authority into Funes.

decisions.decision: Fix the historical assertion type in the subclass through an abstract accessor rather than a constructor field.
decisions.rationale: The observed, declared, and inferred taxonomy stays enforceable and an observation cannot become an inference by changing a value.

decisions.decision: Give the assertion base class a protected decodeState() helper and leave fromArray() to each subclass.
decisions.rationale: Envelope validation and canonical decoding stay in one place without assuming every subclass shares the base constructor signature, and a payload whose serialized type does not match the decoding class is refused.

decisions.decision: Fingerprint the durable assertion fact while excluding its identity and its observation and recording times.
decisions.rationale: Repeated ingestion of the same claim deduplicates while a different tenant, value, source, or assertion type remains a separate fact.

decisions.decision: Express concerns as stateless capability interfaces and assign every concern in the manifesto vocabulary explicitly.
decisions.rationale: A silently omitted concern is indistinguishable from a deliberately excluded one, and stateless interfaces cannot duplicate state the provider-neutral base class already owns.

decisions.decision: Extract shared mechanics into a trait only where the mechanic genuinely repeats across objects.
decisions.rationale: The chronology rule and temporal wire format must match across historical substrate objects for documents to compare and sort; everything else stays private to the object that uses it.

decisions.decision: Do not compose HasSourceLocator separately from HasProvenance on HistoricalAssertion.
decisions.rationale: An assertion's provenance always includes its source locator, and two concerns exposing the same value could disagree.

decisions.decision: Give HistoricalAssertion no provider-family layer and let its three type subclasses extend the provider-neutral base directly.
decisions.rationale: Assertion type and provider family are independent axes, so a family class beneath one type would be wrong for the others and above them would collide with the class-level type invariant; provider mapping belongs to Aleph's acquisition adapters.

decisions.decision: Require every subclass layer to name the axis it partitions, and add none that partitions a second axis.
decisions.rationale: A layer for a second axis is wrong beneath one sibling and collides with the sibling invariant above them; the manifesto's AiModel and Claude shape is a template for acquisition-family objects, not a shape every object must take.

decisions.decision: Make assertion history append-only, tenant-scoped, and reconstructed by transaction time.
decisions.rationale: Immutability makes a re-encounter a duplicate rather than a change, tenant-absent reads avoid leaking existence through errors, and transaction-time reconstruction answers what was known then rather than what is believed now.

decisions.decision: Write assertion timestamp columns as explicit UTC microsecond strings rather than date bindings.
decisions.rationale: The driver's binding format truncates to whole seconds, which would round away history the canonical document preserves; UTC keeps the columns lexicographically comparable across source offsets.

decisions.decision: Keep the assertion type-to-class map in a separate codec rather than on the base class.
decisions.rationale: A base class that knows its own subclasses inverts the dependency the hierarchy exists to establish.

decisions.decision: Route every stored moment through StoredTimestamp as UTC at microsecond precision.
decisions.rationale: The driver's binding dropped the reported offset and truncated to seconds, making one instant indistinguishable from another and leaving ordering, comparison, and point-in-time reconstruction quietly wrong.

decisions.decision: Keep the source's reported offset in the canonical document rather than in the column.
decisions.rationale: Columns exist to filter and order and must be uniformly comparable; the record of what a source said belongs to the document retrieval hydrates from.

decisions.decision: Accept the earlier fidelity of history written before the timestamp precision fix rather than backfill or mark it.
decisions.rationale: The offsets are unrecoverable and could only be guessed, and the data held so far is not yet significant, so a backfill would add machinery and invent precision the records never had.

open_questions: Does HistoricalAssertion need a confidence value for inferred claims, as HistoricalRelationDraft requires, or does evidence alone suffice? The design source assigns HasConfidence to relationships and not to this object, so confidence was left out.
Should declared assertions require a preserved source-field locator, as RelationshipDeclarationDraft does for causal and parent-child relationships?

The MME-2548 ticket template requires AiModelHistoricalAssertion and ClaudeHistoricalAssertion for every object, but the HistoricalAssertion design source lists only observed, declared, and inferred. D-015 follows the design source; confirm the template is boilerplate rather than intent.

Should DeclaredHistoricalAssertion require a preserved namespaced source-field locator and declared value, as RelationshipDeclarationDraft does for causal relationships? Left out for now because the design source does not ask for it.

Should EventAcceptance take a repository interface with a SQL adapter rather than a SqlEventAcceptance subclass of its domain ABC, matching SqlObservationStore and SqlAcceptanceGateway? The design note lists the subclass but its own invariant forbids it.
Should SnapshotObjectReference take a storage-locator adapter rather than ObjectStorageSnapshotReference and DatabaseSnapshotReference subclasses, for the same reason?

The HistoricalEvent design note lists ClaudeHistoricalEvent as a direct subclass of the abstract, but the manifesto requires Claude types to inherit through AiModelHistoricalEvent. Confirm the nesting before MME-2448.

The HistoricalRelationshipAssertion design note names confidence in its purpose but omits HasConfidence from its required concerns. Confirm which is intended, since it also settles the open confidence question on HistoricalAssertion.

MME-2550 asks for round-trip fixtures sourced through Aleph adapters, but those adapters are MME-2549 in a different package. The Funes-side round trip is covered; the shared Aleph-to-Funes conformance fixtures remain blocked on that package.
constraints: Observations and extraction results have no update operation.
Acceptance must remain atomic and safe to retry.
Storage vocabulary must remain independent of a particular website domain.
Entity references must not use host database integers or unqualified display names.
Every new observation must be created in the same transaction as at least one provenance assertion.
Occurrence time cannot be later than observation time.
Producer references and source locators must be non-empty package-owned values.
An external identity claim must reference provenance from the same source.
Cross-source entity equivalence is never inferred from matching display values.
A derived record must reference an existing observation and a named, versioned process.
Observation acceptance never accepts a derived result.
New observed and derived records require a non-empty ingestion-run reference.
Legacy surrogate run references must remain visibly namespaced under funes:legacy and must not be presented as recovered external job identities.
New structured metadata requires a namespaced identifier, non-empty schema version, JSON-encodable attributes, and provenance linkage.
Metadata is excluded from observation identity and has no update or delete operation.
Historical text requires a namespaced kind, content type, non-empty content, optional valid language, and provenance linkage.
The text projection is never authoritative and must be completely rebuildable without provider access.
Cross-package references never depend on another package's model class or private table.
The owning package must authorize every resolution request and return a complete explicit result set.
Snapshots are display and search copies and never replace durable references or canonical owner state.
Entity associations accept only validated roles and durable cross-package references.
Association traversal uses the complete durable reference rather than display values or foreign storage keys.
Historical relationships target only observation, derived-record, or historical-event references.
Internal Funes observation targets must exist before a relationship is accepted.
General historical relationship types do not imply causality or parent-child structure.
Caused-by and child-of relationships cannot be created without a namespaced declaration locator and non-empty declared value.
A declaration assertion must link to the same observation provenance that supplied its relationship.
Every cross-package event requires stable identity, producing package, type, event version, occurrence and recording times, at least one durable subject, and a JSON object payload.
Event occurrence, optional observation, and recording times must be chronological.
Consumers use the event ID as an idempotency key and compare the complete envelope fingerprint before reusing a prior effect.
Delivery is assumed at least once; exact retries cannot create a second canonical consumer effect.
No event contract field implies global ordering; a stream position applies only within its exact stream reference.
Retry and dead-letter metadata cannot mutate or replace the original event.
Funes does not dispatch events, schedule retries, operate dead-letter queues, or own current execution lifecycle state.
The historical assertion contract and its provider-neutral base class name no provider, storage vendor, transport, or framework.
Historical assertion values must be JSON-encodable scalars, null, or arrays; objects and resources are rejected at construction.
Historical assertion predicates must be stable lowercase identifiers and assertion ids must be non-empty opaque values without whitespace.
Historical assertions are readonly; a correction is a new assertion related to the earlier one, never an edit.
A concrete provider assertion class inherits through its provider family and never directly extends the provider-neutral base when a family applies.
A concern interface declares behavior only and never declares state.
Every provider-neutral historical object assigns each of the fifteen manifesto concerns as composed or documented as not applicable with its owner.
No invariant is enforced in more than one place; docs/concerns.md records the single owner of each.
A concern shared across historical substrate objects never names one of them in its members.
No concrete assertion class extends another concrete class; every one extends an abstract parent.
The canonical assertion representation carries a fixed key set and admits no provider-specific payload.
A provider-family layer is introduced only where it adds shared semantics, not because the canonical shape allows one.
A subclass layer is added only after naming both the axis it partitions and the axis the existing layers partition.
Storage mechanism is never a domain-inheritance axis; persistence is supplied through an interface and an adapter.
The assertion store never mutates or deletes; a withdrawal is a tombstone and erasure is a separate concern.
A tombstone requires a reason and preserves the withdrawing authorization context and time.
Assertion retrieval never crosses a tenant boundary and never distinguishes another tenant's evidence from absent evidence.
Valid-time reconstruction over an effective interval is not the assertion store's concern; it reconstructs by transaction time only.
No Sql store binds a raw date object or value to a timestamp column; every write goes through StoredTimestamp.
Stored timestamps are UTC at microsecond precision and are read back as UTC, never in the ambient timezone.
A caller-supplied timestamp string that is not a usable moment is rejected rather than stored.

glossary.source: An external origin identified by an opaque stable reference.
glossary.resource: A canonical address within a source.
glossary.observation: An immutable retrieval of a resource at an observed time.
glossary.discovery: A typed relationship from the observed parent resource to another canonical resource.
glossary.extraction: A versioned success or failure derived from one observation.
glossary.entity_reference: A typed namespaced opaque identifier for a stable cross-application entity.
glossary.source_locator: A source reference, source name, and canonical resource reference sufficient for the owning integration to resolve the original material.
glossary.producer: The stable identity and display name of the package or process that supplied an observation.
glossary.provenance_assertion: An immutable source, producer, temporal, and transformation-lineage path by which Funes knows an observation.
glossary.external_identity: An opaque source-owned identifier retained with the provenance that asserted it.
glossary.stable_entity: A package-owned identity with a durable funes reference reused across historical records.
glossary.observed_record: A source observation accepted through ObservationDraft and always typed observed.
glossary.derived_record: A later process result typed derived and linked to an evidence observation.
glossary.derivation_process: The non-empty process name and version that produced a derived result.
glossary.ingestion_run: A stable host-supplied reference for one connector, process, agent, or ingestion-job execution.
glossary.producer_context: The producer identity and ingestion-run reference through which Funes received or derived a record.
glossary.metadata_assertion: An immutable namespaced, schema-versioned attribute document linked to the provenance that supplied it.
glossary.text_assertion: Immutable namespaced historical text linked to an observation and its accepting provenance.
glossary.text_projection: A disposable adapter-ready copy of authoritative source payload text and text assertions.
glossary.cross_package_reference: A versioned durable value naming an owning package, stable object type, opaque identifier, optional object version, and optional provenance reference.
glossary.reference_snapshot: A non-authoritative display or search copy attached to a durable cross-package reference.
glossary.reference_resolution: An owner-issued available, unavailable, tombstoned, superseded, or unauthorized outcome for one durable reference.
glossary.entity_association: An immutable typed role connecting one historical observation to one durable cross-package entity reference.
glossary.association_provenance: An append-only link recording which observation provenance assertion supplied an entity association fact.
glossary.historical_relationship: An immutable typed link from one observation to another historical event reference without embedding the target record.
glossary.relationship_provenance: An append-only link recording which observation provenance assertion supplied a historical relationship fact.
glossary.relationship_declaration: A preserved namespaced source field and value proving that a source explicitly declared a causal or parent-child relation.
glossary.event_envelope: A versioned immutable cross-package event fact with stable identity, producer, subjects, temporal coordinates, workflow links, provenance, and payload.
glossary.event_fingerprint: The SHA-256 identity of a complete serialized event envelope used to expose conflicting reuse of an event ID.
glossary.event_stream_position: An optional positive sequence scoped to one exact durable stream reference and never a global order.
glossary.delivery_attempt: An immutable started, succeeded, retryable-failure, or dead-lettered outcome associated with an unchanged event ID and fingerprint.
glossary.historical_assertion: One durable claim about a subject reference, carrying a predicate, a value, an assertion type, source and temporal provenance, tenant scope, and evidence.
glossary.assertion_type: Whether a claim was observed at a source, declared by a source, or inferred; fixed by the assertion subclass.
glossary.assertion_fingerprint: A digest of the durable assertion fact excluding its own identity and its observation and recording times, used to deduplicate re-encounters.
glossary.tenant_scope: The organization, user, or explicitly unscoped boundary that owns a piece of evidence.
glossary.concern: A stateless capability interface, optionally paired with a stateless mechanics trait, composed by provider-neutral historical objects.
glossary.concern_register: The docs/concerns.md record assigning every manifesto concern to an object as composed or not applicable, with its reason and real owner.
glossary.invariant_ownership: The rule that each invariant is enforced in exactly one place, recorded per object in the concern register.
glossary.observed_assertion: A claim the history store saw at its source; the source material itself is the evidence.
glossary.declared_assertion: A claim the source explicitly stated rather than merely exhibited.
glossary.inferred_assertion: A claim a later process reasoned its way to; always carries the evidence it was drawn from.
glossary.provider_family: An acquisition or runtime layer between a provider-neutral base and a concrete provider class, introduced only where it adds shared semantics.
glossary.inheritance_axis: The single dimension a subclass layer partitions, such as epistemic status, acquisition family, or subject kind.
glossary.one_axis_rule: The rule that an inheritance chain partitions exactly one axis and a second independent axis belongs in composition or an adapter.
glossary.assertion_disposition: Whether an append stored a first assertion or matched a duplicate; there is no changed case, because assertions are immutable.
glossary.assertion_tombstone: An append-only record withdrawing an assertion from the live view while preserving the claim, the withdrawing context, the time, and the reason.
glossary.transaction_time_reconstruction: Answering what the store knew at a past moment by taking the latest assertion recorded at or before it.
glossary.stored_timestamp: The UTC, microsecond-precision column format for a moment, and the class that is the single authority for writing and reading it.
